claims.statement: NIS2 raises security and reporting requirements and explicitly elevates supply-chain and vulnerability management; ENISA issued detailed implementation guidance in June 2025.
ENISA reports SMEs face budget and skilled-personnel constraints, supporting a current measurable burden from security questionnaires and evidence preparation.
Likely payers are suppliers answering customer assurance requests and regulated buyers reviewing them; which side pays first is unknown.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Supplier security lead or regulated buyer's procurement/security function
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: GRC suites bundle questionnaires; verified reusable evidence for small Polish suppliers and buyer-specific mappings provide resistance
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed supplier subscriptions and buyer-sponsored invitations
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Cybersecurity consultancies, procurement advisers, insurers, and anchor-buyer invitations

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 2,000-8,000 PLN per supplier or 15,000-50,000 PLN per anchor buyer
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Annual supplier fee in advance; buyer implementation prepaid
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 15-50 hours initial supplier evidence assembly
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Security certification, penetration testing, professional liability, and GDPR
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Supplier subscription plus buyer workspace fee
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Evidence review, secure storage, integrations, and partner commissions

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: GRC and procurement platforms introduce lighter supplier portals
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current security-team and supplier labor repeatedly answering questionnaires, collecting controls evidence, and remediating missing documentation
commercial_mechanics.payer: Initially SME technology or industrial suppliers; potentially regulated anchor buyers
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: New customer questionnaire, NIS2 readiness program, tender, or renewal review
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual evidence refresh and each new buyer request

contrary_evidence: NIS2 applicability depends on national implementation and entity classification.
Entrenched GRC suites already serve large buyers.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed data-rights agreement for reusable supplier evidence and buyer-specific sharing permissions; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Sell a local offline evidence pack without exchange or buyer access
critical_control_point.current_owner: Each supplier owns its control evidence; buyers own questionnaire workflows
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed supplier subscriptions and buyer-sponsored invitations
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No supplier evidence or buyer workflow access is currently held
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business after supplier sharing consent; each buyer controls acceptance
critical_control_point.subject: Permissioned reusable supplier-security evidence exchange

economics.acquisition_route: Productize one Polish supplier evidence pack, recruit five suppliers through a cyber adviser, then invite one shared buyer
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 2,000 suppliers at 4,000 PLN ARR produces 8m PLN ARR; network retention and 20% owner earnings could create a 5m PLN net-worth path in 6-9 years. Buyer pull and evidence liability are unknown.
economics.founder_time: 15-25 hours weekly with security review subcontracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Subscriptions less secure storage, evidence review, and customer success
economics.payback: Assumption: 6-12 months for suppliers; longer for anchor buyers
economics.pricing: Assumption: 3,000-10,000 PLN annually per supplier and 20,000-100,000 PLN per buyer workspace
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual refresh plus repeated tender and questionnaire use

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Reusable control mappings and a permissioned supplier-buyer network
fingerprint.customer: Polish SME suppliers to NIS2-affected enterprises
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Supplier or buyer pays to reduce repeated questionnaire and review labor
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Supply-chain security scrutiny expands while SME expertise remains constrained

founder_fit: Structured evidence and automation suit the founder's analytical profile.
Can launch with a narrow questionnaire pack.
Partner-led distribution reduces direct networking intensity.
risks: Sensitive evidence creates a high-value breach target.
Legal applicability and accepted evidence vary by buyer.

structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: supplier evidence profile reused across buyer requests

structure.critical_dependency: Buyer acceptance and secure specialist review

thesis: NIS2-driven supply-chain scrutiny and SME expertise constraints create demand for evidence reuse across buyers rather than repeated spreadsheet questionnaires.
title: NIS2 Vendor Evidence Exchange
uncertainties: Polish transposition details and affected segments require legal validation.
